description:
Eliomilos Museum preserves an old olive mill in the courtyard of the Church of the Saviour in Kakopetria’s historic neighbourhood. The mill is no longer in operation.

Its basin, millstone and pressing equipment illustrate traditional olive-oil production. Local accounts explain how people turned the stone and pressed the crushed olives to extract oil.

A hideout, historical maps, names and other material connect the house with people from the surrounding area. Displays also refer to the community’s experience of the Second World War.

description:
The Ethnographic Museum in Paphos is a private museum based on the collection of George Eliades. Opened in 1958, it occupies a late nineteenth-century stone residence.

Costumes, carved furniture, tools, ceramics, looms and woven objects introduce rural and domestic traditions. Archaeological material adds another dimension to the history of collecting in the Paphos region.

description:
Güzelyurt Railway Station Museum preserves part of the former Cyprus Government Railway’s station complex at Morphou. The station served the area from 1907 until the railway closed in 1951.

Historic station buildings and railway interpretation connect transport with agricultural trade and communications. The site recalls the movement of goods and passengers between Morphou and the rest of the network.

description:
The PEO Historical Labour Museum in Nicosia preserves the history of workers and trade unionism in Cyprus. Founded in 1992, it later moved to a new space in PEO’s premises.

Documents, photographs and historical objects explore working life, labour rights and collective organisation. Interpretation also considers women’s participation and relationships between Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot workers.
